title: Cardiogenic Shock 2026 Update by CSWG
excerpt: A new 2026 report from the Cardiogenic Shock Working Group (CSWG), published in the Journal of Cardiac Failure, proposes an updated staging system designed to make assessment of shock severity simpler, more objective, and applicable across different clinical settings.
body:
Why Was an Update Needed?

The original Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) staging system, introduced in 2019, established a common language for describing cardiogenic shock severity from stage A (at risk) to stage E (extremis).

In 2022, the CSWG introduced more objective thresholds using several clinical variables, including blood pressure, lactate, pH, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and the intensity of circulatory support.

However, some limitations remained:

  • Certain clinical presentations were not adequately captured by existing lactate thresholds.

  • Classification relied on multiple variables, increasing complexity.

  • Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest automatically triggered stage E classification, regardless of subsequent hemodynamic recovery.

  • Treatment intensity and its relationship to severity required further clarification.

The 2026 update addresses these limitations using a much larger contemporary dataset.

The Study: Evidence From Nearly 1.5 Million Patients

Investigators analyzed 11,640 patients enrolled in the multicenter CSWG registry between 2021 and 2025, including patients with heart failure-related cardiogenic shock (HF-CS) and myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (MI-CS).

They examined relationships between clinical parameters, treatment intensity, and in-hospital mortality, including serial measurements during the first 72 hours after shock diagnosis.

The revised classification was then evaluated in an independent population of 1,417,637 patients across 161 hospitals in 20 US states.

The aim was not to create a complex mortality prediction score, but to improve the practicality and consistency of bedside shock classification.
